title: Longest Alternating Subarray After Removing At Most One Element
summary: Given an integer array nums, find the longest alternating subarray after optionally removing at most one element.
statement: Given an integer array nums, find the longest alternating subarray after optionally removing at most one element. An alternating subarray must strictly alternate between greater and smaller values. For example, the subarray must follow one of these patterns: nums[l] nums[l + 2] nums[l + 1] .... A subarray of length 1 is considered alternating. Return the maximum length of such a subarray.
constraints: nums has at least two and up to 100,000 positive values.
After deleting at most one element, select a contiguous subarray of the resulting array.
Adjacent comparisons must be strict and alternate directions.
hints: Precompute alternating run lengths ending at each position for both last comparison directions, and analogous starting lengths.
Without deletion, these arrays give every run; deleting i can stitch positions i-1 and i+1 only when their new comparison has the needed direction.
Combine the matching left and right states without adding the deleted position.
Every optimal result either uses no deletion or has one unique gap, both of which are evaluated with exact direction compatibility.
editorial: Every optimal result either uses no deletion or has one unique gap, both of which are evaluated with exact direction compatibility.

tests.explanation: The entire array already follows >,<,>, so its length is four.
Equal neighbors cannot alternate; a singleton of length one is best.
